figures.alt: A casta painting of a Spanish man, a Black woman, and their child in a shop with hanging meat and poultry.
figures.caption: Anonymous 18th-century casta painting labeled 'De negra y español sale mulato' (From a Black woman and a Spaniard comes a mulatto child).

books.section: Topic 1.5 Labor, Slavery, and Caste in the Spanish Colonial System
The Social Structure of Spanish America
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.misconception: Limits the system to two ancestries the painting goes beyond.
options.text: The system classified only people of Spanish and Indigenous ancestry.
The system also classified children of African descent, giving them a named place.

options.misconception: Confuses naming a rank with ending slavery.
options.text: The system abolished slavery for all children of mixed ancestry.

options.misconception: Claims the law forbade the very classification the painting shows.
options.text: Spanish law prohibited any classification of African-descended people anywhere in the colonies.

rationales.A: This painting classifies African-Spanish parentage, not Indigenous. The system covered more than two ancestries.
rationales.B: The casta system covered everyone in the colonies, including the growing population of African descent. A 'mulato' label shows that children of African and Spanish parents were also sorted into the ancestry hierarchy.
rationales.C: Classification did not abolish slavery or change anyone's legal bondage. A label named a rank; it freed no one.
rationales.D: The painting itself is a classification of an African-descended child. The law sorted these children, it did not forbid sorting them.
rationales.general:
1. Read the label. It names a Black mother, a Spanish father, and a mulato child.
2. Ask what the label proves. The system sorted African-Spanish children too, not only Spanish-Indigenous ones.
3. Ask what it does not prove. A label ranks a child; it does not free anyone or end slavery.
4. Rule out the rest. The system covered African descent, and it classified rather than abolished.
Remember: a label that names a group proves the system reached that group; check who the labels cover.

stimulus.text: This 18th-century casta painting is labeled 'De negra y español sale mulato' — 'From a Black woman and a Spaniard comes a mulatto child.' It shows a Spanish man, a Black woman, and their child in a shop with meat and poultry.
